newsitem.title: USA: Cahners Business Confidence Index fell in November.
newsitem.headline: Cahners Business Confidence Index fell in November.

text.p: Main Street's waning euphoria over President Clinton's re-election weighed heavily on the two-point decline in the Cahners Business Confidence Index (CBCI), according to a report by Cahners Economics.
The CBCI slipped to 65.2 in November from 67.2 in October, the report said.
"It appears that business considered President Clinton's re-election to be a sure bet, and therefore reacted positively in October," Cahners economist Kim Kennedy said.
"By November, the pre-election euphoria was long gone and it was back to business as usual," added Kennedy.
November's two-point drop brought the index back to a "more typical" level, the report said.
Of the 400 manufacturers surveyed, 62.8 percent said they expect the business climate to improve over the next three months, just below the 63.3 percent who said so a year ago.
All seven CBCI components fell in November. The production/sales component declined farthest, falling 4.8 points to stand at 72.2.
Approximately 44 percent of respondents said they plan to hold prices stable in 1997 and another 5.0 percent said they plan to cut prices.
The median price increase anticipated remains below 3.0 percent, the report said.
The CBCI is computed monthly from a telephone survey of 400 senior and mid-level managers in the manufacturing sector.
